fixes.title: OS command injection: untrusted input reaches execSync()
fixes.fix: Replace execSync with execFile and an argv array: execFile("generate-report", ["--for", name]). An argv array removes the shell, but it does not stop argument injection — validate `name` against an allow-list (or pass it after a `--` terminator) so it can't be read as an option.
fixes.patch:
- return execSync("generate-report --for " + name).toString();
+ return execFileSync("generate-report", ["--for", "--", name]).toString();

fixes.title: SQL injection: untrusted input reaches query()
fixes.fix: Bind the value instead of concatenating it, exactly as getUserSafe already does: sqlite.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", [id]).

rootCauses.cause: Request values handed to a helper that builds an interpreter string
rootCauses.note: Both handlers read req.query.* and pass it, unvalidated, to a helper that concatenates it into SQL or a shell command. The fix is structural, not per-site: bind parameters at the data layer and use argv arrays for process execution, then add validation at the route boundary so a future helper inherits neither habit.
